title: Synthetic validation of the chain-HMM forced aligner
hypothesis: A flat-start Baum-Welch chain HMM with 3 states per phoneme recovers phone boundaries on spectrally separable synthetic phones to within 2 frames (20 ms) at a 10 ms hop, and Baum-Welch iterations improve on the flat-start segmentation.

git.status: dirty at run time: src/vhe/data/{features,hmm,aligner}.py and their tests uncommitted

notes: Synthetic only: 30 train utterances of 3-5 band-limited phones, 8 held-out utterances of 4 distinct phones, 3 states/phone, 16 kHz, 10 ms hop. Grid over components (1,2) x iterations (0,1,4). Result: 1 component recovers every interior boundary within 12 ms (mean 5.9 ms) at flat start and 11.8 ms after 4 EM passes, so the 20 ms gate passes; 2 components are worse (26 ms). Baum-Welch raises likelihood monotonically (16378 -> 25429 nats) but does not improve boundaries (mean error 5.9 -> 9.7 ms), so the predicted EM gain is falsified on this fixture and the fixture cannot rank configurations. Five development bugs recorded in the README (state-id scope, repeated-index scatter, variance floor, unvisited states, iterations=0 silently running one pass). No real speech, no training, no listening.
